title: Higher even-moment coefficient tail
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\mu$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, let $X\colon\Omega\to\mathbb R$, let $r,j\in\mathbb N$, and let $t\in\mathbb R$. If $g_l$ denotes the even-moment coefficient gap for $\mu$, $X$, $r$, and $l$, the higher even-moment coefficient tail is $\sum_{l=0}^{r} -g_l t^{2l-2j}$ over indices with $j<l$, with a zero summand for all other indices.
caveat: The supplied snippet does not include the definition of the even-moment coefficient gap, so its mathematical meaning cannot be specified more fully.
